record.original_question: For conditional rewrite systems, under what syntactic restrictions does parallel rewriting enjoy subcommutativity, a strong form of confluence analogous to the subcommutativity of parallel rewriting in orthogonal term-rewriting systems?

evidence.quote: Which conditional rewrite systems are subcommutative?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. A term rewriting system (TRS) is a set R of rewrite rules ℓ → r over terms built from a signature and a set of variables. The one-step rewrite relation →_R is defined by ℓσ →_R rσ at any position of a term. The parallel rewrite relation ⇒_R reduces a finite set of pairwise-disjoint (parallel) redex positions simultaneously. A binary relation → is called subcommutative (or has the diamond property) if whenever a → b and a → c there exists d with b → d and c → d. For an orthogonal TRS (left-linear, no critical pairs) the parallel rewrite relation ⇒_R is known to be subcommutative, which gives a strong form of confluence.

A conditional term rewriting system (CTRS) is a set of conditional rules of the form ℓ → r ⇐ s₁ ≈ t₁, …, s_n ≈ t_n, where the conditions s_i ≈ t_i are interpreted (depending on the type of CTRS, e.g., join, oriented, semi-equational, or normal) as requirements that have to hold for a rewrite step using the rule to be valid. The corresponding rewrite relation is defined inductively in levels: →_0 = ∅, and a step at level k+1 uses rules whose conditions are satisfied with respect to →_k. The parallel rewrite relation ⇒_R for a CTRS is defined analogously by contracting pairwise-disjoint parallel redexes (each licensed by the appropriate conditional inference).

Problem. Determine syntactic conditions on a conditional term rewriting system R (such as restrictions on left-linearity, on the variables occurring in the conditions and right-hand sides, on critical pairs of the underlying unconditional system, on the form of the conditions, or on the type of CTRS) under which the parallel rewrite relation ⇒_R is subcommutative, i.e. satisfies: whenever t ⇒_R u and t ⇒_R v, there exists w with u ⇒_R w and v ⇒_R w. Equivalently, characterize the classes of CTRSs for which subcommutativity of parallel rewriting holds, in analogy with the orthogonal (unconditional) case.
artifact.status_search_result: Existing literature establishes various confluence criteria for conditional term rewriting systems (level-confluence, shallow confluence, confluence modulo, etc.), but no general syntactic characterization of subcommutativity of parallel rewriting for CTRSs analogous to the orthogonal-TRS case appears to have been published. The question remains listed as an open problem and no resolution was found in the search.

status_evidence.title: Level-Confluence of Conditional Rewrite Systems
status_evidence.snippet: Stratification of conditional rewrite relations leads to fine-grained notions of confluence; shallow confluence implies level confluence which implies confluence.
status_evidence.claim: Confluence notions for CTRSs are stratified, but a syntactic subcommutativity criterion for parallel rewriting is not given.

status_evidence.title: Confluence of conditional rewriting modulo
status_evidence.snippet: Results for standard conditional rewrite systems extend to oriented and level-confluent natural systems; it would be interesting to know if certain restrictions can be dropped.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work identifies open questions surrounding confluence/parallel-step properties for CTRSs.
